scope: Proposition 7.1 of the manuscript “The Blockwise Alperin Weight Conjecture” (preprints/The-Blockwise-Alperin-Weight-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 202 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 042c7730f058d508), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 45-46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose Op(J) = 1 and (7.1) holds. There is no finite extension L/Ks with [L : Ks]p < ph over which the marked curve X = XL admits a geometrically connected smooth 45 projective J-Galois cover f : Y → X, with its J-action defined over L, branched only at the marked points and with ramification index divisible by p at every marked point.
